config.title: WebSocket Hook

intro.title: WebSocket Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook that manages a WebSocket connection. You will learn how to use the useEffect hook to establish and clean up a WebSocket, and the useState hook to store and update real-time messages. The main technologies involved are React hooks, the WebSocket API, and event listeners. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that can connect to a WebSocket server and handle incoming data.
intro.usecase: WebSocket hooks are essential for building real-time features in modern web applications. You'll see them powering live chat interfaces like Slack or Discord, where messages appear instantly without page refreshes. They're also crucial for financial dashboards displaying live stock prices, collaborative editing tools like Google Docs showing real-time cursor positions, and multiplayer game interfaces updating player movements immediately. As a developer, implementing WebSocket hooks lets you create responsive, interactive experiences that feel alive and connected.

objectives: Implement a custom React hook to manage WebSocket connections
Initialize WebSocket connections with dynamic URL parameters
Control WebSocket lifecycle events (open, message, close, error) within React components
Manipulate component state based on real-time WebSocket data
Bind WebSocket event handlers to update UI components
Integrate the WebSocket hook into a functional React component
Configure message sending and receiving through the custom hook interface
Apply cleanup logic to properly close WebSocket connections on component unmount

steps.title: Import React and required hooks (useState, useEffect, useRef)
steps.instruction: Import React, useState, useEffect, and useRef from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary modules from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the useWebSocket custom hook function
steps.instruction: Create a custom hook function named useWebSocket that takes a URL parameter and returns an empty object.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts a URL parameter and returns an object. For now, just return an empty object {}.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';

// Create the useWebSocket custom hook function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A useWebSocket function is defined that takes a URL parameter and returns an empty object.
successCriteria: The useWebSocket function is created with a URL parameter and returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function is named useWebSocket, accepts a URL parameter, and returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check the function name, parameter, and return value.

steps.title: Initialize state for WebSocket connection status
steps.instruction: Inside the useWebSocket function, use useState to create an 'isConnected' state variable initialized to false.
steps.hint: Call useState with the initial value false and destructure the returned array into a variable and setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useWebSocket function will have an isConnected state variable that tracks the WebSocket connection status.
successCriteria: The useWebSocket function contains a useState call that creates an isConnected variable initialized to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState with the correct initial value and destructuring pattern.
steps.feedbackWrong: The isConnected state variable wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use useState(false) inside the useWebSocket function.

steps.title: Initialize state for WebSocket messages
steps.instruction: Inside the useWebSocket function, add a useState call to create a 'messages' state variable initialized to an empty array.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The initial value should be an empty array [].
steps.expectedOutcome: The useWebSocket function will have a 'messages' state variable ready to store incoming WebSocket messages.
successCriteria: The useWebSocket function contains a useState call that declares a 'messages' variable initialized to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an empty array as the initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside useWebSocket, use useState to create a 'messages' state variable initialized to [].

steps.title: Create a ref to store the WebSocket instance
steps.instruction: Inside the useWebSocket function, create a ref using useRef to store the WebSocket instance. Initialize it to null.
steps.hint: Use the useRef hook you imported earlier to create a reference that persists across renders.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a ref for a DOM element
const inputRef = useRef(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The useWebSocket function will contain a socketRef variable created with useRef, initialized to null.
successCriteria: A socketRef variable is created using useRef and initialized to null inside the useWebSocket function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useRef to create the reference and initializing it to null inside the useWebSocket function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the useWebSocket function, use the useRef hook to create a reference for the WebSocket instance and set its initial value to null.

steps.title: Return the hook's interface object
steps.instruction: Return an object from the useWebSocket hook containing isConnected, messages, and disconnect function so consuming components can access them.
steps.hint: At the end of your hook function, use a return statement with an object containing the three values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The hook now exposes its state and functionality through a returned object, making it ready for components to consume.
successCriteria: The useWebSocket hook returns an object containing isConnected, messages, and disconnect function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning an object with exactly isConnected, messages, and disconnect.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook isn't returning the required interface. Check that you're returning an object with the three properties.
